Playbook.name: QA - USB/CD Allow/Block Changes - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1091 Replication Through Removable Media
MITRE ATT and CK T1052.001 Exfiltration over USB

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Kaspersky Device Control recorded USB / CD-DVD connect decisions on an endpoint - a device was Allowed (GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUGGED) or Blocked (GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUG_DENIED). The event message carries the device category, the bus type ("USB (except mice and keyboards)", CD/DVD, etc.), the user and the Result Decision (Allow / Block). Two signals matter: an Allowed removable / optical device on a sensitive host (a data-exfiltration or malware-introduction vector), and repeated Blocked attempts by one user (a device-control circumvention attempt). Although this rule is named with the QA prefix, it is treated here as a production device-control audit.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Removable and optical media are primary vectors for exfiltrating customer / PCI data and for introducing malware onto bank endpoints. Device-control decisions are the enforcement record; an allowed device on a sensitive host, or persistent bypass attempts, require confirmation.

Assets.AssetType: Windows / endpoints managed by Kaspersky Device Control

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Kaspersky Security Center CEF (verified live on logs-cef.log-*, cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab", observer.product "SecurityCenter"). Fields: destination.domain (the affected ENDPOINT, not the collector), destination.user.name (initiator, e.g. INTDOM\user or NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM), cef.device.event_class_id (GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUGGED = Allow, GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUG_DENIED = Block, GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_UNPLUGGED = removed), cef.name ("Device is connected" / block), cef.severity, message and cef.extensions.message (multi-line: Device category, Device type/Bus type, User, Result Decision, Result Operation). Pivot on destination.domain as the host of interest.

Signal.Name: USB/CD Allow/Block Changes
Signal.Details: Kaspersky Device Control USB / optical connect Allow or Block decisions on an endpoint.

Input.name: $endpoint
Input.description: Endpoint hostname (destination.domain), e.g. SME-TV4. Matches the alert entity.

ImmediateCapture.Item: Note the Allow vs Block split and the device type (USB storage vs CD/DVD vs other) from the message.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance. An Allowed storage device on a sensitive host, or a burst of Blocks by one user, matters more than the raw event count.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the device-control activity is routine enforcement, an allowed removable device that needs a data-handling review, or repeated bypass attempts.

Step.name: Allow vs Block posture on the endpoint
Step.Purpose: Break the endpoint's device-control decisions into Allowed / Blocked / Removed with the users involved.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND cef.device.event_class_id IN ("GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUGGED","GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUG_DENIED","GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_UNPLUGGED") AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(destination.user.name), signals = VALUES(cef.name) BY cef.device.event_class_id | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: DEV_PLUG_DENIED dominating = device control enforcing policy (usually benign). DEV_PLUGGED (Allow) on a restricted host, or a mix driven by one user rapidly retrying, points to the review cases below.

Step.name: Allowed device connections (potential exfil / malware vector)
Step.Purpose: Detail the devices that were permitted - the message reveals the device category, bus type (USB / CD-DVD) and the user.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUGGED" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, destination.user.name, cef.name, cef.severity, observer.product, message | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Read the message: "Device type/Bus type" tells USB mass storage vs CD/DVD vs other; "User" is the active user; "Result Decision: Allow" confirms the device was permitted. An allowed mass-storage / optical device by an unexpected user on a sensitive host is the data-handling review case. System-user allows for internal buses are routine.

Step.name: Blocked attempts (device-control circumvention)
Step.Purpose: Detail the denied connect attempts - repeated blocks by one user can indicate attempts to bypass device control.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_DEVCTRL_DEV_PLUG_DENIED" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, destination.user.name, cef.name, cef.severity, message | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A few blocks = policy working (benign). Many blocks by the same user across different devices, or persistent retries, indicate a deliberate attempt to attach unauthorised media - review the user. Read the message device type to see what they tried to connect.

Node.Condition: An Allowed removable / optical device by an unexpected user on a restricted / sensitive host, or a burst of Blocked attempts indicating deliberate device-control circumvention.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unsanctioned media use or circumvention attempt - data-handling / user review)

Node.Condition: Blocked attempts only (device control enforced the policy), or expected Allowed device use by an authorised user per policy.
Node.Result: False Positive (Policy enforced, or authorised device use)

Node.Condition: Device-control policy is over-permissive (allowing storage it should block) or over-restrictive (blocking a legitimately needed device).
An allowed device or repeated-block pattern whose legitimacy cannot be determined from the logs alone.

FalsePositive.Definition: Device control working as designed, or authorised device use.

Indicators.Item: Allowed device is a sanctioned, asset-registered device used by its assigned user.
System-user allow of an internal bus.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the block outcome or the device's sanctioned status; close as policy_enforced_or_authorised (not "benign").

TruePositive.Definition: Unsanctioned removable / optical media use, or a circumvention attempt.

Indicators.Item: Allowed storage / optical device by an unexpected user on a restricted host.
Many blocked attempts by one user across devices (bypass attempts).
Exfiltration / malware context on the host.

SOCAction.Item: Review what data was accessible; interview the user; scan the host for malware from the media; tighten the device-control policy; escalate if exfiltration is suspected.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An over-permissive or over-restrictive device-control policy.

Indicators.Item: Storage repeatedly allowed where policy intends a block.
A legitimately needed device repeatedly blocked for a valid user.

SOCAction.Item: Raise a device-control policy-tuning request with the device details; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Establish the Allow / Block split and the device types; identify the user(s) and whether the host is sensitive.
For an Allowed removable / optical device by an unexpected user, or a burst of blocks by one user, capture the message details and begin a data-handling / user review.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Review data accessible on the allowed device; interview the user; scan the host for malware introduced from the media; tighten device-control policy for the endpoint / group.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce removable-media encryption and whitelisting; maintain an approved-device register; review device-control policy scope; educate users; document lessons learned.

Escalation.Trigger: An Allowed removable / optical device by an unexpected user on a sensitive host, persistent bypass attempts, or evidence of data copied to media.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Block outcome or sanctioned-device use confirmed and documented; policy-tuning request raised if the policy was mis-scoped.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unsanctioned media / circumvention scoped; data exposure assessed; host scanned; user addressed; device-control policy tightened; case recorded (IR opened if exfiltration / malware confirmed).
